summary: The counting explanation and prevalence comparison are well supported, but the decisive spoken probability is numerically wrong and conflicts with the planned visual result.

issues.detail: The Reveal says 'Nine out of a hundred eight: ninety percent.' Recalculation gives 9/108 = 1/12, approximately 8.3%, not 90%. This is the central requested result and contradicts the visual fraction and the subsequent distinction from sensitivity. Correct the spoken result to approximately 8.3% while preserving the explanation that all 108 positives form the denominator; regenerate any dependent audio/timing after editing speech.

checks: The supplied rates recompute to 9/10 = 90% sensitivity and 99/990 = 10% false-positive rate; the positive total is 108.
The second population correctly gives 90 true positives and 90 false positives with rates fixed, hence 90/180 = 50%.
The regrouping operation preserves condition colors and adds a separate test-result encoding, exposing why conditioning changes the denominator.
Exactly three scenes include one explicitly invited six-second pause; the fraction and probability are withheld until its Reveal.

363 spoken words plus six seconds of silence estimate approximately 166-198 seconds at 150-125 words per minute with the prescribed allowance, consistent with roughly three minutes; audio timing was not measured.
The narrative labels the example hypothetical and nonmedical, introduces the changed population explicitly, preserves cohort totals and keeps interactions empty.
